_comment: Sacred locations. Coordinates are approximate centroids of the named site (verify before production). 'religion_ids' lists every tradition with significant ties to the place (e.g. Jerusalem spans three). 'primary_religion_id' is the dominant association for default map coloring.

locations.name: Mecca
locations.summary: Holiest city in Islam, home of the Kaaba and the destination of the Hajj pilgrimage.

locations.name: Medina (Yathrib)
locations.summary: City the Prophet Muhammad migrated to in 622 CE; site of the first mosque and his tomb.

locations.name: Cave of Hira
locations.summary: Cave where, in Islamic tradition, Muhammad received the first revelation of the Qur'an.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.summary: A city sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, encompassing the Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif, the Western Wall, and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

locations.name: Karbala
locations.summary: Site of the Battle of Karbala (680 CE) and a major pilgrimage center, especially in Shia Islam.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.summary: Traditional birthplace of Jesus, marked by the Church of the Nativity.

locations.name: Nazareth
locations.summary: Town associated with the childhood of Jesus and the Annunciation in Christian tradition.

locations.name: Sea of Galilee
locations.summary: Region of much of Jesus' ministry in the Gospels.

locations.name: Rome
locations.summary: Center of the early Western church and, later, the seat of the papacy at Vatican City.

locations.name: Damascus
locations.summary: Site of Paul's conversion in Christian tradition and a major early Islamic capital under the Umayyads.

locations.name: Nicaea
locations.summary: Site of the First Council of Nicaea (325 CE), an early defining council of the Christian church.

locations.name: Mount Sinai
locations.summary: Mountain where, in tradition, Moses received the Torah. The traditional location is debated.

locations.name: Hebron
locations.summary: Home of the Cave of the Patriarchs, traditional burial place of Abraham and other patriarchs.

locations.name: Ur
locations.summary: Ancient Mesopotamian city named in tradition as Abraham's place of origin.

locations.name: Babylon
locations.summary: Destination of the Babylonian exile of Judeans after the destruction of the First Temple.

locations.name: Varanasi (Kashi)
locations.summary: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, sacred to Shiva and a major Hindu pilgrimage site on the Ganges.

locations.name: Ayodhya
locations.summary: Traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Rama and a major center in the Ramayana.

locations.name: Mathura
locations.summary: Traditional birthplace of Krishna and a center of Krishna devotion.

locations.name: Kurukshetra
locations.summary: Traditional setting of the Mahabharata war and the Bhagavad Gita's dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna.

locations.name: Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam)
locations.summary: Confluence of the Ganges and Yamuna rivers; a principal site of the Kumbh Mela pilgrimage.

locations.name: Haridwar
locations.summary: Sacred Ganges pilgrimage city and one of the rotating sites of the Kumbh Mela.

locations.name: Nankana Sahib
locations.summary: Birthplace of Guru Nanak (formerly Rai Bhoi di Talwandi), a major Sikh pilgrimage site.

locations.name: Kartarpur
locations.summary: Where Guru Nanak established a community and spent his final years; site of Gurdwara Darbar Sahib.

locations.name: Amritsar
locations.summary: Home of the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), the holiest site in Sikhism.

locations.name: Anandpur Sahib
locations.summary: Where Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699.

locations.name: Patna Sahib
locations.summary: Birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh; site of Takht Sri Patna Sahib.

locations.name: Lumbini
locations.summary: Traditional birthplace of the Buddha and a UNESCO World Heritage pilgrimage site.

locations.name: Bodh Gaya
locations.summary: Site of the Buddha's enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree; home of the Mahabodhi Temple.

locations.name: Sarnath
locations.summary: Deer Park where the Buddha gave his first sermon, setting the 'wheel of dharma' in motion.

locations.name: Kushinagar
locations.summary: Where the Buddha entered parinirvana (final passing) in Buddhist tradition.

locations.name: Sanchi
locations.summary: Home of the Great Stupa, among the oldest stone structures in India, associated with Emperor Ashoka.

locations.name: Ise Grand Shrine
locations.summary: The most sacred Shinto shrine, dedicated to the sun goddess Amaterasu, ritually rebuilt every 20 years.

locations.name: Izumo Taisha
locations.summary: One of Japan's oldest and most important Shinto shrines, associated with the kami Okuninushi.

locations.name: Mount Fuji
locations.summary: A sacred mountain long venerated in Shinto and Buddhist practice and a site of pilgrimage.

locations.name: Itsukushima Shrine
locations.summary: Shrine famous for its 'floating' torii gate, dedicated to kami of seas and storms.

locations.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
locations.summary: Head shrine of the kami Inari, famous for its thousands of vermilion torii gates.
